title: Return 200 with null fields for 'not applicable' state, not 404
answers: Should an endpoint return 404 when a feature doesn't apply to a project?
Why does events_retention return null instead of 404?
body:
Review on the events retention endpoint established: don't use 404 to signal 'feature/window not enabled'. 404 must keep meaning 'no such project or no access', and every non-2xx response is captured as a `client_request_failure` event, so a per-insight banner call would spam it while a rollout flag is off.
- Pattern: always 200; window fields null (`EventsRetentionSerializer` with `allow_null=True` in products/product_analytics/backend/presentation/events_retention.py).
- Frontend consumer `loadRetentionMonths` in frontend/src/scenes/insights/dataRetention/dataRetentionBannerLogic.ts treats null as 'not enforced' and has no 404 catch.
- Avoid an 'enforced' boolean next to the values; null conveys it without looking like a setting.
applies: New DRF endpoints whose data may not apply to a project, especially ones polled by frontend logics

search: Return 200 with null fields instead of 404 when a feature or data window does not apply to a project; 404 must signal 'no such project or no access', and every non-2xx response is captured as `client_request_failure` event, causing spam when polled by frontend. Use `allow_null=True` in serializers like `EventsRetentionSerializer` in `products/product_analytics/backend/presentation/events_retention.py:EventsRetentionViewSet.list`. Do not add an 'enforced' boolean alongside null values; null itself conveys 'not applicable'. Frontend consumer `loadRetentionMonths` in `frontend/src/scenes/insights/dataRetention/dataRetentionBannerLogic.ts` treats null as 'not enforced' and has no 404 catch. Applies to DRF endpoints whose data may not apply to a project, especially those polled by frontend logics.
